items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: There was a black guy that stayed with us the longest, and even this was a northern tour, it wasn't a southern tour, it was Trummy Young.

ctx.x: No; even the stars that we had, they weren't with us in the south; they were up with us in the north, plus the fact that they weren't regulars of the band. They would be brought in for a date, a theater date or a recording session, a week shot somewhere, but that was it, and none of them were regulars.

There was a black guy that stayed with us the longest, and even this was a northern tour, it wasn't a southern tour, it was Trummy Young. He was with us--I don't remember how long, but it was a prolonged period of time. I think at least six or more months.
The other guys, Bird, Diz, Benny Harris, Pettiford, whoever else, they were in for a few days, a weekend, but not down south.

items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: He had a piano player that wrote real good. His name was John Handy -- George Handy.

ctx.x: Did you record with them? (inaudible)? Or you didn't record with Boyd Raeburn?

No. I didn't record with Raeburn. No, I didn't -- I didn't record with Raeburn. I played a few jobs with him, though, you know. He had a piano player that wrote real good. His name was John Handy -- George Handy.
